z: 韁 ubende, umthambo, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
The old practice of sitting with the sick, of keeping watch, of not filling the air, is this turn. Do not rush to be useful. Be there.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 韁 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to perform a talk.

z: 韃 ubende, umthambo, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
The wisdom shared by many houses is hard: do not let the sun go down on a break you are willing to heal, and do not call it healing if you are only waiting to retell it.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 韃 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Name the break once, without extra charges. Then do one small trustworthy thing, and repeat it tomorrow.

z: 韆 ubende, umthambo, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Children grieve in strange hours and then ask for ordinary things. Both are grief. Answer the ordinary thing. Do not make them perform a sadness you can recognize.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 韆 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Do not hurry a grieving person into cheer. Let the absent name be said.

z: 韈 ubende, umthambo, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A child who sees an adult look again, after a bad day, learns that a bad day is not a verdict. This is worth more than any optimism you could announce.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 韈 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Open the curtain before you decide what the day is. Let the house see you do it.

z: 韉 ubende, umthambo, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Children are the usual casualties of a score kept between adults. They did not agree to carry it. Mercy toward the person you resent is also protection of the child.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 韉 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Do one undeserved kindness where you are keeping score. Do not mention the score.

z: 韋 ubende, umthambo, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Siblings fight because they share a roof and a hunger. The fight is not the failure. The failure is when the stronger one discovers a liking for the smaller one's fear. Protection refuses that discovery.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 韋 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: When the heat rises, name who you are actually keeping safe. Put your body between the danger and the child. Do not spend the heat on the child.

z: 韌 ubende, umthambo, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Brothers and sisters are the first public. What you do to be admired at home becomes the way they will treat their own children. Give them a dignity they can copy.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 韌 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Once, take the lower seat on purpose. Let someone in the house finish a story you could have told better.

z: 韑 ubende, umthambo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
The teachings that endured all warn the eye. They also bless the eye that rejoices. Rejoicing is not a mood. It is a decision made again each time the other person shines.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 韑 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Clap, or thank, before you comment. Let the first sound from you be glad.

z: 韓 ubende, umthambo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Fear of the future makes a house small. Courage does not enlarge the future. It keeps today's people inside the house while the future remains unknown.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 韓 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Tell the truth you have been saving, and remain in the room after it is told.

z: 韔 ubende, umthambo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Psychology is simple here. The closed hand teaches the body that the world is about to run out. The open hand teaches it that tomorrow includes other people.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 韔 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Put one thing you were keeping back into the middle of the table.

z: 韘 ubende, umthambo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Gossip is how a house talks about its own when they have left the room. Healing speech waits until they are back, and then says the hard thing to the face, cleanly.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 韘 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: If you gave someone a cruel name, retire it today, out loud, and do not use it again.

z: 韙 ubende, umthambo, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Across the old writings, the warning against scoffing is constant. A scoffer cannot be taught, and a house that scoffs cannot learn itself.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 韙 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Look at one ordinary object they mended or prepared, and say what it cost them.

z: 韛 ubende, umthambo, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Some truths are not ready for speech. Presence holds them without using them as a weapon. A weaponized silence is still a weapon.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 韛 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: If your quiet has been a punishment, break it with one gentle sentence and then stay.

z: 韜 ubende, umthambo, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
A child who watches a break become a lifelong trial learns that love is a court. A child who watches a break become a mended bowl learns that love can survive its own failure.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 韜 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: If you were the one who broke trust, say what you did without a speech about why it was almost fair.

z: 韞 ubende, umthambo, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Compassion is grief that has recognized itself in another body and does not hurry it. Hurry is fear. The unhurried hour is the gift.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 韞 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Answer the ordinary request of a grieving child. Do not make them perform a sadness you recognize.

z: 韡 ubende, umthambo, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
The sciences of a lasting household call this resilience. The older word is faithfulness. It does not deny the dark. It refuses to let the dark be the only speaker.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 韡 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Decline the word forever. Keep the true sentence about the pain, and stop before the lie.

z: 韭 ubende, umthambo, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Many sacred traditions, in different grammars, say the same hard thing: the injury stops when someone declines to pass it on. This is not weakness. It is the end of a chain.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 韭 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Tell the truth of the wrong once, to the person, and then do not serve it at breakfast.

z: 韮 ubende, umthambo, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
At the table, anger wants the last word. The last word is rarely food. Let the sentence end before it becomes the story the children will tell about this house.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 韮 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: If you have already burned someone you love, say so before the day ends, and then do one ordinary kindness with your hands.

z: 韱 ubende, umthambo, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The guest at the table is a test you did not schedule. If your worth requires the guest to be less clever, less beautiful, less faithful, your worth is a costume. Take it off.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. ubende, umthambo, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 韱 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Kneel, or sit, so your eyes meet a child's. Stay there until the conversation is theirs.

z: 韲 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
What you wish were yours, name it exactly, in the hearing of the person who has it. Then do not reach. The naming is the confession. The not-reaching is the turn.

practice: Ask the person to show you how they did the thing. Be a student for ten minutes.

z: 韴 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Name the loss you are counting. Often it is a person in the room, not a disaster outside. Then put your body beside that person. That is the whole practice.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 韴 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Hold the doorway. Let the frightened one see that you are not leaving.

z: 韵 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Give before you calculate whether you will be thanked. Thanks are not the food. If you require them, you have made a trade, and a trade is not yet a family.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 韵 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Give a thing away that you still like. Do not wait until you are tired of it.

z: 韶 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Wisdom is not silence forever. There is a time to speak. The test is whether the words can be repeated in front of the person, and still be a kindness.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 韶 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Tell one story tonight in which a person in this house is repaired, not mocked.

z: 韻 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Look at the work you have stopped seeing. Name it. The naming is not flattery. It is the return of sight, and sight is the turn.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 韻 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Ask to be shown a skill you had decided was beneath you. Watch the whole way through.

z: 響 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to be interesting. You do have to be in the house.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 響 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Be findable. Tell the house which room you will be in, and be in it.

z: 頁 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Accountability is the first half. Without it, forgiveness is a fog. The one who broke the trust says what was done, without a speech about why it was almost justified.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 頁 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

z: 頂 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The oldest writings are full of lament, not because lament is holy by itself, but because love that cannot lament becomes hard. Let the house be soft enough to cry.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 頂 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Leave the empty place unspoken-of only if the grieving person wishes it. Otherwise, speak the name.

z: 頃 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Despair often tells the truth about pain and then adds a lie about forever. Keep the truth. Decline the forever. Forever is not a fact available to a person at a window.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 頃 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

z: 頄 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Accountability remains. Mercy is not the cancellation of truth. It is the decision that truth will not be used as a knife at breakfast for the next twenty years.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 頄 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Do one undeserved kindness where you are keeping score. Do not mention the score.

z: 項 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
An elder who has turned anger into protection does not become mild. The wall is still warm. What changes is the face it turns toward. It faces the street, not the cradle.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 項 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: When the heat rises, name who you are actually keeping safe. Put your body between the danger and the child. Do not spend the heat on the child.

z: 順 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder's dignity is not the right to be obeyed in every small thing. It is the right to be respected while still listening. The listening is what makes the respect true.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 順 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Once, take the lower seat on purpose. Let someone in the house finish a story you could have told better.

z: 頊 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Across generations, envy of the young is fear of being finished. Admiration of the young is how an elder stays in the story without owning it.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 頊 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Say out loud, in the hearing of the person, the exact good you wished were yours. Then leave it theirs.

z: 頌 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder who has been afraid and stayed is a better teacher than an elder who claims never to have shaken. The shaking, survived, is the lesson.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 頌 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Stay until the scared person is breathing slowly. Do not explain the dark away before you have sat in it.

z: 頍 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
An elder who gives the best piece away is not being careless with the future. The elder is showing the future how a house continues.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 頍 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Pass the best portion first. The first piece teaches the house what it is.

z: 頎 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder's stories are a kind of speech that builds or bends a family. Tell the story in which people are repaired. The other story will tell itself.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 頎 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Speak the true sentence. Keep the second one, the one that only wanted to win.

z: 頏 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
An elder who still notices the small faithfulness in the house is a gift to the young. The young become what is noticed.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 頏 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.

z: 預 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder's quiet can be a shelter or a locked door. The young can tell which, by whether they are welcome to come and say nothing beside you.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 預 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: If your quiet has been a punishment, break it with one gentle sentence and then stay.

z: 頑 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Some breaks end a household. That too can be told with dignity. Forgiveness then is the refusal to poison the years that follow. The children still have to live in them.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla is the place this turning becomes visible. 頑 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.

z: 頒 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder who speaks of the dead by name, without recruiting the young into despair, gives the family its memory and its future in the same breath.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 頒 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Bring food. Take the lower seat. Stay past the moment you become uncomfortable.

z: 頓 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
An elder who has looked again, many mornings, is a quiet argument against the lie. Do not turn the elder into a slogan. Let the morning itself be seen.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu is the place this turning becomes visible. 頓 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.
practice: Make one plan for tomorrow small enough that both of you can keep it.

z: 頔 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder who lays down a feud gives the young a future that is not already written. That is one of the last great gifts a generation can give the next.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele is the place this turning becomes visible. 頔 marks the page and leaves the anatomy clear, because wisdom that hides the body is not yet wisdom.

z: 頖 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Anger is the house defending itself before it has measured the threat. Left alone, it burns the people it meant to keep. The heat is not the enemy. Direction is. Turned, the same heat stands in the doorway so the small ones can sleep.

practice: Before the second loud sentence, step into the doorway, not toward the person. Let the heat guard the house from outside.

z: 頗 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Pride needs an audience and a person beneath it. Dignity needs neither. Hidden inside pride is the refusal to be nothing. That refusal is good. It becomes poison only when someone else must be smaller for it to stand.

z: 領 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Envy is love of a good thing, twisted until the good thing must shrink. The love was real. That is why it hurts. Turned, the same look becomes admiration, which is fed by another person's light.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. Look long enough at iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 領 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.

z: 頚 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Fear is the mind counting what it loves and what it could lose. That count is not a defect. It is proof of attachment, and attachment is how a family exists. Courage is fear that stays in the room.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. Look long enough at iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 頚 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Hold the doorway. Let the frightened one see that you are not leaving.

z: 頞 iphaphu, amabhamuza amaphaphu, ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla

Many houses, under many names, give the same command: do not be ruled by dread, and do not despise the person who is. The strong are asked to stay, not to sneer.

line:

z: 颶 ngesibonakhulu, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Siblings remember the name they were called on the worst day. Do not give them that name. Give them the name of the good you have actually seen them do.

line:
Children who are met with contempt learn to hide the clumsy part, which is most of them. Appreciation gives that part a chair.

z: 颸 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
The old practice of sitting with the sick, of keeping watch, of not filling the air, is this turn. Do not rush to be useful. Be there.

z: 颺 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
The wisdom shared by many houses is hard: do not let the sun go down on a break you are willing to heal, and do not call it healing if you are only waiting to retell it.

z: 颻 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu

Children grieve in strange hours and then ask for ordinary things. Both are grief. Answer the ordinary thing. Do not make them perform a sadness you can recognize.

z: 颼 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A child who sees an adult look again, after a bad day, learns that a bad day is not a verdict. This is worth more than any optimism you could announce.

z: 颿 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Children are the usual casualties of a score kept between adults. They did not agree to carry it. Mercy toward the person you resent is also protection of the child.

z: 飂 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Siblings fight because they share a roof and a hunger. The fight is not the failure. The failure is when the stronger one discovers a liking for the smaller one's fear. Protection refuses that discovery.

z: 飃 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Brothers and sisters are the first public. What you do to be admired at home becomes the way they will treat their own children. Give them a dignity they can copy.

z: 飄 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu

The teachings that endured all warn the eye. They also bless the eye that rejoices. Rejoicing is not a mood. It is a decision made again each time the other person shines.

z: 飆 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Fear of the future makes a house small. Courage does not enlarge the future. It keeps today's people inside the house while the future remains unknown.

practice: Hold the doorway. Let the frightened one see that you are not leaving.

z: 飇 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Psychology is simple here. The closed hand teaches the body that the world is about to run out. The open hand teaches it that tomorrow includes other people.

z: 飈 ngesibonakhulu, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Gossip is how a house talks about its own when they have left the room. Healing speech waits until they are back, and then says the hard thing to the face, cleanly.

z: 飋 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Across the old writings, the warning against scoffing is constant. A scoffer cannot be taught, and a house that scoffs cannot learn itself.

practice: Ask to be shown a skill you had decided was beneath you. Watch the whole way through.

z: 飛 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Some truths are not ready for speech. Presence holds them without using them as a weapon. A weaponized silence is still a weapon.

practice: Be findable. Tell the house which room you will be in, and be in it.

z: 飜 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
A child who watches a break become a lifelong trial learns that love is a court. A child who watches a break become a mended bowl learns that love can survive its own failure.

practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

z: 食 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Compassion is grief that has recognized itself in another body and does not hurry it. Hurry is fear. The unhurried hour is the gift.

practice: Leave the empty place unspoken-of only if the grieving person wishes it. Otherwise, speak the name.

z: 飠 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
The sciences of a lasting household call this resilience. The older word is faithfulness. It does not deny the dark. It refuses to let the dark be the only speaker.

practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

z: 飡 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Many sacred traditions, in different grammars, say the same hard thing: the injury stops when someone declines to pass it on. This is not weakness. It is the end of a chain.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. Look long enough at ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 飡 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Do one undeserved kindness where you are keeping score. Do not mention the score.

z: 飢 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
At the table, anger wants the last word. The last word is rarely food. Let the sentence end before it becomes the story the children will tell about this house.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. Look long enough at ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 飢 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: When the heat rises, name who you are actually keeping safe. Put your body between the danger and the child. Do not spend the heat on the child.

z: 飣 ngesibonakhulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The guest at the table is a test you did not schedule. If your worth requires the guest to be less clever, less beautiful, less faithful, your worth is a costume. Take it off.

practice: Once, take the lower seat on purpose. Let someone in the house finish a story you could have told better.

z: 飥 izindlala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
What you wish were yours, name it exactly, in the hearing of the person who has it. Then do not reach. The naming is the confession. The not-reaching is the turn.

practice: Say out loud, in the hearing of the person, the exact good you wished were yours. Then leave it theirs.

z: 飧 izindlala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Name the loss you are counting. Often it is a person in the room, not a disaster outside. Then put your body beside that person. That is the whole practice.

practice: Stay until the scared person is breathing slowly. Do not explain the dark away before you have sat in it.

z: 飩 izindlala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Give before you calculate whether you will be thanked. Thanks are not the food. If you require them, you have made a trade, and a trade is not yet a family.

practice: Pass the best portion first. The first piece teaches the house what it is.

z: 飪 izindlala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Wisdom is not silence forever. There is a time to speak. The test is whether the words can be repeated in front of the person, and still be a kindness.

practice: Speak the true sentence. Keep the second one, the one that only wanted to win.

z: 飫 izindlala, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Look at the work you have stopped seeing. Name it. The naming is not flattery. It is the return of sight, and sight is the turn.

practice: Look at one ordinary object they mended or prepared, and say what it cost them.

z: 飭 izindlala, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to be interesting. You do have to be in the house.

z: 飮 izindlala, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Accountability is the first half. Without it, forgiveness is a fog. The one who broke the trust says what was done, without a speech about why it was almost justified.

practice: If you were the one who broke trust, say what you did without a speech about why it was almost fair.

z: 飯 izindlala, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The oldest writings are full of lament, not because lament is holy by itself, but because love that cannot lament becomes hard. Let the house be soft enough to cry.

practice: Bring food. Take the lower seat. Stay past the moment you become uncomfortable.

z: 飰 izindlala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Despair often tells the truth about pain and then adds a lie about forever. Keep the truth. Decline the forever. Forever is not a fact available to a person at a window.

practice: Make one plan for tomorrow small enough that both of you can keep it.

z: 飱 izindlala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Accountability remains. Mercy is not the cancellation of truth. It is the decision that truth will not be used as a knife at breakfast for the next twenty years.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. Look long enough at izindlala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 飱 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Leave one cut unanswered today. Do not announce the leaving.

z: 飲 izindlala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
An elder who has turned anger into protection does not become mild. The wall is still warm. What changes is the face it turns toward. It faces the street, not the cradle.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. Look long enough at izindlala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 飲 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Before the second loud sentence, step into the doorway, not toward the person. Let the heat guard the house from outside.

z: 飳 izindlala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder's dignity is not the right to be obeyed in every small thing. It is the right to be respected while still listening. The listening is what makes the respect true.

practice: Kneel, or sit, so your eyes meet a child's. Stay there until the conversation is theirs.

z: 飴 izindlala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Across generations, envy of the young is fear of being finished. Admiration of the young is how an elder stays in the story without owning it.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. Look long enough at izindlala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 飴 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Ask the person to show you how they did the thing. Be a student for ten minutes.

z: 飼 izindlala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder who has been afraid and stayed is a better teacher than an elder who claims never to have shaken. The shaking, survived, is the lesson.

practice: Hold the doorway. Let the frightened one see that you are not leaving.

z: 飽 izindlala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
An elder who gives the best piece away is not being careless with the future. The elder is showing the future how a house continues.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. Look long enough at izindlala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 飽 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Feed the guest, or the youngest, before you take your own share.

z: 飾 izindlala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder's stories are a kind of speech that builds or bends a family. Tell the story in which people are repaired. The other story will tell itself.

practice: Say the hard thing to the face, once, cleanly, with no audience.

z: 餃 izindlala, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
An elder who still notices the small faithfulness in the house is a gift to the young. The young become what is noticed.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. Look long enough at izindlala, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 餃 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Remove the sneer from a sentence and speak it again. Notice how much of it was only the sneer.

z: 餅 izindlala, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder's quiet can be a shelter or a locked door. The young can tell which, by whether they are welcome to come and say nothing beside you.

practice: Sit with a person who is not ready to speak. Let ten minutes pass without fixing them.

z: 餈 izindlala, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Some breaks end a household. That too can be told with dignity. Forgiveness then is the refusal to poison the years that follow. The children still have to live in them.

practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

z: 餉 izindlala, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder who speaks of the dead by name, without recruiting the young into despair, gives the family its memory and its future in the same breath.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. Look long enough at izindlala, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 餉 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.

z: 養 izindlala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
An elder who has looked again, many mornings, is a quiet argument against the lie. Do not turn the elder into a slogan. Let the morning itself be seen.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. Look long enough at izindlala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 養 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

z: 餌 izindlala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder who lays down a feud gives the young a future that is not already written. That is one of the last great gifts a generation can give the next.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. Look long enough at izindlala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 餌 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: If a child is carrying a feud that belongs to adults, take it back. Say that it is not theirs.

z: 餐 izindlala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Anger is the house defending itself before it has measured the threat. Left alone, it burns the people it meant to keep. The heat is not the enemy. Direction is. Turned, the same heat stands in the doorway so the small ones can sleep.

practice: Teach the strong child to stand in front of the smaller one. That is anger, turned, and it can be learned young.

z: 餒 izindlala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Pride needs an audience and a person beneath it. Dignity needs neither. Hidden inside pride is the refusal to be nothing. That refusal is good. It becomes poison only when someone else must be smaller for it to stand.

practice: Praise a person in the house for a quality you do not share. Do not add a correction.

z: 餓 izindlala, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Envy is love of a good thing, twisted until the good thing must shrink. The love was real. That is why it hurts. Turned, the same look becomes admiration, which is fed by another person's light.

practice: When a sibling is praised, add one true sentence of your own. Do not balance it with your own news.

z: 餔 izindlala, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Fear is the mind counting what it loves and what it could lose. That count is not a defect. It is proof of attachment, and attachment is how a family exists. Courage is fear that stays in the room.

This is the work of welcoming a guest. A successful family is a body that can still use every member. izindlala, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele is included. 餔 is included. Neither is asked to disappear so the other can be admired.

z: 餖 izindlala, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
